findings.title: 已完成前轮与下一轮准入之间退出会搁置 active Goal
fact: Original Bus/SQLite recovery probe left an active unmet Goal with automaticState completed and an empty Inbox; recover returned no Session while manual advance immediately admitted the next round.
After the minimal completed-outcome guard repair, the same probe returns the Session, preserves one pending input and two rounds, and manual advance reports waiting.
findings.hypothesis: Exit between durable completion of a Goal round and the runner next advance loses the only entry responsible for admitting the unfinished successor round.
findings.inference: The original recover guard excludes completed outcomes at goal.ts:1367. Restart recovery consumes Goal parents at execution/restart.ts:215, while automaticState at input-result.ts:138 classifies fully terminal owned results as completed and execution/restart.ts:239 releases that claim. Reusing the existing advance at goal.ts:1374 admits the required successor under the existing Goal policy.
findings.recommendation: Allow completed outcomes through the existing recover-to-advance path; keep condition, budget, selection and admission deduplication with the existing advance owner.
findings.idempotency: Repeated recover can emit the same advisory wake for an existing pending input. The verified invariant is no duplicate Goal round or inbox admission.

findings.title: Retry hooks replacing decision are discarded by the prepared-request bridge
fact: policy-level red keepers fail for both primary and compaction delay replacement and decline
PluginHooks.trigger returns the supplied mutable event; the bridge supplied a clone and discarded the returned decision
findings.hypothesis: Adding producing connection through an object spread separated the policy decision object from the hook decision object.
findings.inference: SessionRunnerRetry.policy reads the original event after awaiting input.hook, while SessionModelRequest.prepare.retry had passed a clone and asVoid discarded the mutation.
findings.recommendation: Copy the returned mutable decision back to the policy event; preserve connection metadata and existing retry API.

findings.title: Synchronous Task self-target waits on an input that only its own blocked runner can promote
fact: Original TaskTool/Session runner admitted a self-target queue input, stayed active, and did not reach idle after durable readiness.
The same original plugin setup also makes automatic title requests, which are separately routed in the probe.
findings.hypothesis: The foreground Task waits for its self-target result, blocking the tools fan-in required before the next provider-turn/input boundary.
findings.inference: TaskTool.dispatchRoot calls waitTaskOperation before Tool settlement; SessionStep awaits all tool fibers; the same Session runner promotes another input only after that settlement. The observed input remains pending while that chain is waiting.
findings.recommendation: Reject only synchronous self-target dispatch before reservation, using the existing ControllerConflictError/ToolFailure path. Preserve background and admit-only self-target queue admission.
